newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Yoshimoto Kogyo to make comedies in Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Yoshimoto Kogyo to make comedies in Asia.

text.p: Japanese entertainment company Yoshimoto Kogyo Co Ltd says it is planning to build another movie theatre in Tokyo and produce comedies and animated movies in Asia as part of an overall business expansion.
Company president Hideo Nakamura said in a recent interview with Reuters that it would also branch into programming for broadcasters.
Yoshimoto manages vaudeville theatres and produces television and radio shows.
Nakamura said the company's earnings for the six months to September 30 will fall short of its forecast but it is still on track to meet its full-year earnings target for the year to March 31, 1998.
The firm said in May it expected a parent current profit of 2.50 billion yen on revenues of 25.30 billion yen in 1997/98.
In 1996/97, it posted an actual parent current profit of 2.43 billion yen on revenues of 23.22 billion yen.

Asked if it plans to raise its annual dividend, Nakamura said: "It all depends on our business results, although we are making efforts to raise our annual dividend to 10 yen. We would also like to improve our benefits to shareholders by, for example, giving them free tickets to our events."
Yoshimoto said in May that it would pay a nine yen dividend in 1997/98, unchanged from 1996/97.
Nakamura said the company is looking to expand in the entertainment field in Tokyo and across Asia.
"It may be difficult for us to open theatres in Asia due to language problems but we hope to make comedies and animated movies in Asia, where production costs are low," Nakamura said.
Yoshimoto has already agreed with Hong Kong's Golden Harvest Entertainment to jointly produce a martial arts comedy, he said.
"We can make a movie in Hong Kong at about 200 million yen, about half the production cost in Japan," Nakamura said.
Yoshimoto also hopes to open a second theatre in Tokyo in 2000/01.
The theatre will probably have more than 1,000 seats but details will be decided by the end of March 1998, he said.
Nakamura added that Yoshimoto formed in April a unit to research and produce programmes for broadcasters.
He said: "Media will change over the next few years. We need to know which types of media and which broadcasters will be strong in the industry."
